transcript:
Header: 2025-12-29 16:00 PST | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Miguel Torres (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Horizon Head of ML), Ethan Cole (Horizon SRE), Sam Bennett (Horizon Product)

Summary:
Short demo/walkthrough of Redwood's Eval & Quality Monitoring. Focus on how prompt sets are versioned, how regression alerts fire on metric drift, and how A/B comparisons between model variants are automated. Customer interested in pilot for safety/quality checks and integration with their CI.

00:00 - 00:18 Ava: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, this is Ava from Redwood, with Miguel our solutions engineer. Today we'll show the Eval and quality monitoring flow — prompt sets, automated regressions, A/B comparisons and the Console + API hooks. Can everyone hear me?
00:19 - 00:27 Priya: Yep, can hear you.
00:28 - 01:02 Miguel: Cool, quick agenda — 1) Console walkthrough for prompt set management, 2) Demo of regression alerts and thresholds, 3) A/B compare and rollout example, 4) Q&A and next steps. We'll keep it hands on.
01:03 - 01:22 Ethan: For context, our main blockers are reproducible regressions after model upgrades and getting early alerts before customers see bad outputs. Latency is a secondary concern but cost matters.
01:23 - 01:40 Sam: Also we need a hook into our CI so that any release triggers an eval job and fails gating if quality drops.
01:41 - 02:06 Miguel: Perfect, that's exactly what Redwood Optimize + Eval monitoring are built for — you can store prompt sets, label golden responses, define metrics (exact match, ROUGE, semantic-similarity via embeddings), and set alert rules. We'll show a demo using a retail Q&A prompt set similar to yours.
02:07 - 03:00 Miguel: (screen share) Starting in the Console, here's the Eval tab — this is where teams upload prompt sets. You can create suites, tag them, pin a baseline model, and upload expected outputs. Quick note: the UI sometimes shows Redwood Optimise spelled differently in older builds, ignore that — it's the same product.
03:01 - 04:12 Priya: When you say "pin a baseline model" what does that do technically? Does it pin to model hash/version so we can compare to future variants?
04:13 - 05:05 Miguel: Yes, it pins to a model version id and stores the baseline outputs. When a new model is rolled out, the system runs the same prompt set against the candidate and computes diff metrics. You can pick metrics like semantic-similarity (cosine on embeddings), token-level changes, and custom regex checks for safety.
05:06 - 06:22 Priya: How are embeddings computed? We use a custom in-house embedder currently; can we plug that in?
06:23 - 07:10 Miguel: You can bring your own embeddings — Redwood's eval can accept precomputed vectors in the upload or it can compute using Redwood-verified embedding models. For consistency we recommend precomputing in CI to avoid vendor drift.
07:11 - 08:05 Ethan: On the infra side — for sensitive data we need the eval to run inside our VPC or on Dedicated. Does the eval runner support Private deployments?
08:06 - 09:02 Miguel: Yes, Redwood Private supports running eval jobs entirely in-customer with a private control plane. For the hosted pilot we'll run in Redwood's hosted infra with data retention disabled, but for production you can move to Dedicated or Private.
09:03 - 11:00 Miguel: (demo) Here's creating a regression alert: pick a metric (semantic-similarity), set baseline threshold (0.85), set alert to trigger if average drops by >5% across suite. It can send webhook, PagerDuty, or create an issue in Jira. You can attach a sample diff that shows top failing prompts.
11:01 - 12:30 Priya: Can we alert on per-prompt failures too? We have a small set of high-priority prompts we want immediate notifications for.
12:31 - 13:20 Miguel: Yep, you can create per-prompt rules, and set severity. Also can configure rolling windows (last 1k requests) vs nightly batch.
13:21 - 15:00 Sam: Walk me through A/B comparisons. We want to do canary rollouts between quantized and full models and measure degradation on certain intents.
15:01 - 17:25 Miguel: (screen) A/B compare allows you to run two model variants against same prompt set. Redwood will compute paired-difference stats, confidence intervals, and highlight statistically significant regressions. You can select traffic split and auto-fail a rollout if key metrics drop beyond X. There's an API endpoint and Console view.
17:26 - 18:40 Priya: How long does it take to run a full suite of 10k prompts? We're trying to budget time for nightly runs.
18:41 - 19:30 Miguel: On hosted Redwood, typical throughput depends on model size and batching; a 10k suite for a medium LLM can finish in under an hour with continuous batching — for Dedicated you'll get predictable time. We'll provide an estimated runner in the benchmark script.
19:31 - 21:00 Ethan: Integration with CI — can Redwood kick off evals via our pipeline and then return pass/fail as exit code?
21:01 - 22:18 Miguel: Yes, the Redwood CLI returns status codes and we have a REST API to trigger eval jobs. We also provide a GitHub Action that uploads prompt sets, runs eval, and fails the workflow if thresholds are breached.
22:19 - 24:00 Priya: Security questions — do you keep request logs? We need audit logs but also need to ensure PII is redacted and keys never leave our KMS.
24:01 - 25:40 Ava: We support customer-managed KMS in Private mode, and audit logs are configurable. For hosted pilots we can disable retention and enable encryption; SOC2 reports will be shared. For enterprise, logs can be routed to your SIEM.
25:41 - 27:10 Sam: Any customers doing model regression alerts in production?
27:11 - 28:05 Ava: Yes, a few fintech and healthcare customers use this daily; they link alerts into their oncall and gate releases. We can share an anonymized case study.
28:06 - 31:00 Miguel: (demo) Show a failing prompt example: baseline answer vs candidate, metric drop from 0.92 to 0.74. Console highlights changed tokens and semantic drift. Also shows suggestions — e.g., add context to prompt or fallback to earlier model variant.
31:01 - 33:20 Priya: Does the system support A/B on reranking models / multi-step pipelines? We have a reranker upstream and generation downstream.
33:21 - 34:40 Miguel: You can evaluate full pipeline by uploading the intermediate stage outputs, or run evals per component and then an end-to-end suite. We also support composite metrics.
34:41 - 36:00 Ethan: Cost — what's the unit economics for running nightly suites?
36:01 - 37:12 Ava: Cost depends on model size and whether you use Hosted vs Dedicated. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantized variants for evals to save cost while keeping fidelity; we'll include a cost estimate in the pilot pack.
37:13 - 39:00 Sam: For pilot success criteria — Priya and I propose: 1) auto-regression detection for our high-priority 200 prompts with false-positive rate <10%, 2) CI integration that gates releases, 3) benchmark showing no more than 5% average latency increase when enabling evals.
39:01 - 41:00 Priya: That sounds right. Also we'd like webhook payload sample and example alert card.
41:01 - 43:00 Miguel: We'll send webhook examples and sample JSON. Also provide instructions for running the Redwood CLI in a sandbox with your creds masked.
43:01 - 44:20 Ava: Quick recap — we'll send security docs, pilot pricing, benchmark scripts, and a starter prompt-set template. Miguel will run initial benchmark with your sample prompts once Priya uploads them.
44:21 - 44:50 Priya: Great, thanks. Looking forward to the pilot.
44:51 - 45:00 Ava: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up via email with next steps.

Notes on transcript quality: auto transcription had a few mis-hearings ("Optimise" vs "Optimize", "KV cache" occasionally transcribed as "K V cache"). There was some crosstalk during the demo screenshare.
